Think of the airway as the passage air takes to reach your lungs. When you fall asleep, the muscles in your throat relax. For someone with obstructive sleep apnea, that passage can narrow or close repeatedly. Breathing pauses briefly, then starts again. A sleep study helps a physician find out whether that's happening.
